Action Plan:
1. Arrange urgent hospital assessment today for acute onset shortness of breath in a 4-week post-cesarean patient; patient will self-transport immediately with her baby.
2. Educate patient about risk of post-partum venous thrombo-embolism (possible pulmonary embolism); explained need for ED tests and potential anticoagulation.
3. Offer ambulance transfer; patient declined, prefers own transport.
4. Advise to withhold further codeine until reviewed in hospital.
5. Remind patient to take essentials for baby and attend ED promptly; partner to meet her there if possible.
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden shortness of breath for ~1 hour while resting and watching TV.  
• Associated symptoms: Dry cough since yesterday; palpitations; mild chest soreness on deep inspiration; no frank chest pain, hemoptysis, leg pain/swelling, fever.  
• Onset/progression: Acute onset; no prior similar episodes; not clearly worsening over the hour.  
• Past medical/surgical history: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; no other chronic illnesses reported.  
• Medications: Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented); last taken ≈1 week ago.  
• Allergies: Ibuprofen – reaction not specified.  
• Family history: Mother with history of leg clots (DVT).  
• Social history: Lives with partner (at work currently); caring for 4-week-old infant; smoking/alcohol not discussed.

Objective:
• Pulse (patient self-counted radial): 30 beats counted over ~15 s → estimated ~120 bpm (tachycardic).  
• No further vitals or physical examination documented.  
• No investigations performed during consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute shortness of breath, 4 weeks post-cesarean:  
   – Assessment / likely diagnosis: Pulmonary embolism (High likelihood – DDx item “Pulmonary embolism (post-partum)” [High]).  
   – Differentials:  
     • Acute respiratory infection / pneumonia (Medium – DDx).  
     • Anxiety/panic attack (Medium – DDx).  
     • Peripartum cardiomyopathy (Low-Medium – DDx).  
   – Investigations planned: To be performed in ED (likely D-dimer, CTPA/VQ scan, ECG, CXR, bloods) – not performed during telehealth.  
   – Treatment planned: Immediate ED referral; possible anticoagulation pending work-up (explained to patient).  
   – Relevant referrals: Emergency Department today.

2. Post-operative pain management / Codeine use:  
   – Assessment: Currently off codeine for 1 week; advised temporary cessation until hospital review.  
   – Treatment planned: Hold codeine; reassess need and safety after hospital evaluation.  
   – No investigations or referrals required at present.

3. Medication allergy: Ibuprofen  
   – Assessment: NSAID allergy noted; reaction details unclear.  
   – Plan: Document allergy; avoid NSAIDs; clarify reaction at future visit.

Quality checks:
• Missing but clinically expected elements: Full vital signs (BP, RR, SpO₂, temperature), cardiopulmonary examination, smoking/alcohol history, full obstetric/gynecologic history, clarification of ibuprofen reaction, complete medication list with doses.  
• Internal conflicts: Date of birth recorded as 20 Apr 1980 by patient; clinician repeated 1983 (conflict noted).  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor pauses/over-talk; no inaudible sections affecting clinical data.
